findings.reason: Confirmed (high). Theorem 3 (published pp. 265–266) lists '(i) 2 representations of PGL2 generated by the eigenforms in S24(SL2(Z))', which share their weights ±23/2, and then ends 'They are all self-dual (symplectic) and uniquely determined by their weights'. Item theorem-3 and route 1's brief copy that final sentence. The fix, uniqueness for (ii)–(iv) only and multiplicity two in (i), with a new sourceIssue, is right.

Confirmed (high). The definition on p. 264 reads 'for all i ≠ j we have either w_i ≠ w_j, or m ≡ 0 mod 4, i = j − 1 = m/2 and w_i = w_j = 0'. The quantifier ranges over ordered pairs while the exception is oriented. With two central zeros, the pair (j, i) = (m/2 + 1, m/2) is not covered, so no w with a double zero is regular, although §2.2 (p. 274) intends the double-zero case. Item W-m-regular copies the definition. The fix, quantifying over i < j or using {i, j} = {m/2, m/2 + 1}, with a sourceIssue, is right.

Confirmed (high) for existence. Item regular-w-unique-G states 'Every regular w ∈ W_m, m ≥ 1, is of the form w(λ) for a unique split classical group G … and a dominant weight λ', after p. 268 ('any regular w in W_m … is of the form w(λ) for a unique split classical group G over Z and some dominant weight λ'). The regular (1, −1) ∈ W_2 is not of this form. The only group with n_G = 2 is SO_3, whose w(λ) = (λ_1 + 1/2, −λ_1 − 1/2) is half-integral. On uniqueness, the item asserts only that G is unique, but footnote 5's |λ_n| ≤ λ_{n−1} for SO_{2n} means λ is determined only up to the outer automorphism, so any reading as a unique pair also fails. The fix, restricting to the image of the formulas and imposing λ_n ≥ 0 for SO_{2n} as p. 292 does, is right.

Confirmed (high). The rendered pages show B_f^F(π, π′) = ℜ Σ_{p,k} F(k log p)(log p/p^{k/2}) \overline{tr(c_p(π)^k)} tr(c_p(π′)^k) (p. 275), and J_F(U) = −∫_R (Γ′/Γ)(1/2 + 2πit, U) F̂(t) dt ((2.3.4), p. 276). Item explicit-formula-forms drops the real part and the conjugate in B_f and integrates against F(t) instead of F̂(t). Item C-F-and-POS states POS with 'F̂(ξ) ≥ 0' at complex ξ, where Definition 2.1 has the real part. These change the objects of the positivity method. The fix is right.

Confirmed (high). (2.4.3) (p. 278) allows U = (U_i) ∈ K_∞^r with no restriction, and (2.4.4) uses F̂(0)δ_iδ_j(1 − ε(U_i·U_j))/4. By p. 274, ε(I_w) = i^{w+1}, so ε takes values in {±1, ±i}, and the red team's choice U_1 = 1, U_2 = ε gives ε(U_1·U_2) = i. The off-diagonal entry is then nonreal, so β_Q is not a real symmetric form and 'least eigenvalue' and 'minimum' are undefined. Item quadratic-problem copies the unrestricted domain. The fix, restricting to U_i for which ε(U_i·U_j) = ±1 (for example determinant-one parameters, which covers the paper's applications), with a sourceIssue, is right.

Confirmed (high). Page 302 says the 2g + 1 eigenvalues 0, ±(k_i − i) 'are distinct if, and only if, we have k_g > g', and item holomorphic-lowest-weight copies this. For g = 1 and k = (0), the trivial representation, which exists as ρ_k, the eigenvalues are 0, ±1, all distinct, while k_g = 0 is not greater than 1. The 'only if' fails, though k_g > g does imply distinctness. The fix, an exact criterion via a_i = k_i − i with a sourceIssue, is right.

Confirmed (high). Page 312 prints ψ_G = ψ_F ⊕ [n − 2g_0 − 1] for n > 2g_0 + 1 and ψ_F = ψ_G ⊕ [2g_0 + 1 − n] for n < 2g_0 + 1, with F = ϑ_g(G). Since dim ψ_F = 2g + 1 and dim ψ_G = n, these force g = g_0. Lemma 5.8 on the same page gives ψ_F = ψ_G ⊕ [2g − n + 1] for the higher lifts. Item theta-series-properties copies the g_0 form. The fix, using g, or scoping the printed relation to the first occurrence g = g_0, is right.

Confirmed, though I would grade it medium: it is a wrong library status and interface, not a false mathematical statement. Item split-classical-groups (status library) defines the split classical groups as group schemes over Z, but cites only point groups (Matrix.symplecticGroup and TauCeti.QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroup/specialOrthogonalGroup). At Tau Ceti f790474, TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Symplectic/Basic.lean has the symplectic group scheme (groupScheme) and pointsMulEquiv, and Symplectic/Smooth.lean has instSmoothCoordinateHopfAlgebra over every commutative ring. So the Sp scheme exists and should be reused, while the split SO model over Z, especially at 2, is not the cited point group. The fix is right.

Confirmed (medium). Page 271 prints tr(c_i | V_k) = sin((2k+1)π/i)/sin(2π/i). At k = 0 this gives sin(π/i)/sin(2π/i) ≠ 1 (for example 1/√2 at i = 4), against the trivial character, and the denominator vanishes at i = 2. Item so3-example silently uses sin(π/i). The fix, keeping the item and recording a sourceIssue, is right.

Confirmed (medium). Page 270 cites 'Siegel's theorem on the rationality of the values of Artin L-functions at non-negative integers'. The theorem concerns non-positive integers, and ζ(2) = π²/6 shows the printed range is wrong. The item note gives the corrected range as if quoting. The fix, labelling the correction and adding a sourceIssue, is right.

Confirmed (medium), on the text and the red team's counting argument; I did not rerun the enumeration. Page 309 says 'We find exactly 199 such parameters … only 59 of these 199 do satisfy this formula', in the setting 1 ≤ g ≤ 12. Item section-5-3-1 states these counts in that setting while its note says they count shapes, including genus zero and with Δ¹₂₃ and Δ²₂₃ collapsed. Whatever the exact corrected numbers, a statement and a note that disagree on what is counted is an error. The fix, stating the counting convention explicitly and recording the scope discrepancy, is right.

Confirmed (medium). data/restructure/RS-07.result.json gives AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.6 the action 'drop' and assigns 'Zero counts, explicit formulas, zero-density estimates and RH/GRH statement interface' to AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3, formerly AN.6.
